Yes, that's the right behavior. For day-to-day use I wouldn't want to log in every single time — staying signed in on normal visits is what I'd expect. But if I've been away long enough that the session's gone stale, asking me to sign in again is sensible; that's the kind of thing that keeps a private collection private.

And I really like the two details you added. Dropping me back into the same view after I sign in — rather than dumping me at some generic home screen and making me find my place again — is thoughtful. And if I was halfway through writing a note or editing something, holding onto that text so I don't lose it is exactly right. Just as important: *not* quietly saving it for me. If I hadn't hit save yet, I'd want it handed back to me to finish and save myself, not committed behind my back. That respects that I hadn't decided yet. Good — this matches my intent. Let's keep going.
